test_name: Headline Test: Feature vs Benefit Focus

hypothesis.statement: If we change the headline from 'Project Management Software for Teams' to 'Ship Projects 2x Faster,' then CTR will improve by ≥10% because benefit-focused headlines addressing outcomes (speed) outperform feature-focused headlines (software type) based on competitive analysis and direct response copywriting principles.
hypothesis.basis: Competitor observation, established copywriting best practices, aligns with user intent (people want outcomes, not tools)

control.headline: Project Management Software for Teams
control.description: Feature-focused, describes what the product is

test_design.isolation_confirmed: Only headline 1 differs between variations. All other headlines, descriptions, and ad settings remain identical.

statistical_requirements.note: With 21-day constraint, you'll have ~4,725 clicks per variation. This gives ~75% power to detect 10% improvement, or full power to detect 12% improvement. Acceptable tradeoff given business constraint.

secondary_metrics.reason: Higher CTR is worthless if it attracts wrong audience

guardrails.reason: Ensures we're not sacrificing efficiency for vanity clicks

decision_rules.winner: Variation CTR ≥10% higher with 95% confidence AND guardrails pass
decision_rules.loser: Variation CTR lower OR guardrails fail
decision_rules.inconclusive: CTR improvement <10% or confidence <95% - extend test or accept null

implementation_notes: Create new RSA with variation headline pinned to position 1
Keep all other headlines identical to control
Enable experiment in Google Ads (campaign experiment feature)
Verify both ads serving on Day 1
monitoring_checkpoints: Day 1-2: Verify both variations receiving traffic
Day 14: Review data quality, note any anomalies
do_not: Check results daily hoping for early winner
Stop test early even if one variation looks better
Change anything else in the campaign during test

risks_and_considerations.risk: Benefit claim may attract browsers, not buyers
risks_and_considerations.mitigation: CVR guardrail metric will catch this
Accepting 12% MDE at full power, or 10% MDE at 75% power
Document any known events, promotions, or competitor changes

pre_test.test_name: Headline Test: Feature vs Benefit Focus
pre_test.hypothesis: Benefit-focused headline will improve CTR by ≥10%
